text:
Predicates:
Register(x) ::: x can register to vote in the United States.
Participate(x) ::: x can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
Citizen(x, y) ::: x has citizenship of y.
Official(x, y) ::: x is an official of y.
Manager(x, y) ::: x is a manager at y.
Premises:
∀x (Register(x) → Participate(x)) ::: Everyone who can register to vote in the United States can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
∀x (Citizen(x, unitedStates) → Register(x)) ::: If someone has United States citizenship, then they can register to vote in the United States.
∀x (Citizen(x, unitedStates) ⊕ Citizen(x, taiwan)) ::: A person either has United States citizenship or Taiwanese citizenship.
∀x (Official(x, russianFederation) → ¬Citizen(x, taiwan)) ::: No Russian Federation officials hold Taiwanese citizenship.
¬Citizen(vladimir, taiwan) ∧ ¬Manager(vladimir, gazprom) ::: Vladimir neither holds Taiwanese citizenship nor is he a manager at Gazprom.
Register(ekaterina) ⊕ Official(ekaterina, russianFederation) ::: Ekaterina can register to vote in the United States, or she is a Russian Federation official.
Conclusion:
Participate(ekaterina) ∨ Manager(ekaterina, gazprom) ::: Ekaterina can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election or is a manager at Gazprom.
